description: Councils: every council the site files elections, offices or boundaries under. Pre-1973 Northern Ireland councils are each their own elections body (id = body slug); the 26 district councils of 1973 and the 11 of 2014 share the local-government body; the Republic's city and county councils share ireland-local. Nothing here is invented: each field comes from a source listed below, and a date or name no source gives is absent. Schema: registries/schemas/councils.schema.json; views: registries/councils.mjs.
sources: scripts/lib/election-names.mjs (era titles, plain titles, pre-1973 bodies, year-dated titles)
data/offices/offices.json and scripts/ingest/facts/ef_offices.py (official names, offices institutions)
Published sources for the research of 7 Nov 2026 (refactor round 2): citations, cited as cite:<id>

census-1926-fermanagh.title: Census of Northern Ireland 1926: County of Fermanagh
census-1926-fermanagh.cites: p. vii, Administrative Divisions, changes since 1911: (g) Belleek Rural District abolished and its area added to Irvinestown Rural District (1 April 1921); (h) Clones No. 2 Rural District abolished and its area added to Lisnaskea Rural District (1 April 1921).

census-1926-tyrone.title: Census of Northern Ireland 1926: County of Tyrone
census-1926-tyrone.cites: p. vi, Administrative Divisions, changes since 1911: (a) Trillick Rural District abolished and its area added to Omagh Rural District (1 April 1920).

srno-ni-1967-57.title: New Towns (Municipal Functions—Craigavon) Order (Northern Ireland) 1967, S.R. & O. (N.I.) 1967 No. 57
srno-ni-1967-57.cites: Art. 2 (the appointed day is 1 April 1967); art. 4 (from that day the Craigavon Development Commission exercises the functions of an urban district council for the whole of the Rural District of Lurgan except the part in Schedule 1, and that area is called "the Urban District of Craigavon"); art. 5 (the Schedule 1 part is added to the Borough of Lurgan).

srno-ni-1969-62.title: Londonderry Area (Municipal Functions—Londonderry Rural District) Order (Northern Ireland) 1969, S.R. & O. (N.I.) 1969 No. 62
srno-ni-1969-62.cites: Art. 2 (the appointed day is 2 April 1969); art. 4(1) (from that day the Londonderry Development Commission exercises the functions of an urban district council for the area of the Rural District of Londonderry, and that area is called "the Urban District of Londonderry").

lgba-ni-2008-s1.title: Local Government (Boundaries) Act (Northern Ireland) 2008, section 1
lgba-ni-2008-s1.cites: s. 1(1)-(2): Northern Ireland is divided into 11 districts, each incorporating the whole or the major part of the former districts listed for it; district 6 is Belfast. In operation in full from 1 April 2015.

uksi-2013-3156.title: S.I. 2013/3156, "Temporary modifications to facilitate transition from the existing councils to the new councils"
uksi-2013-3156.cites: Art. 4(1): existing councillors retire together on 1 April 2015; art. 8: the existing and the new councils sit side by side from the 2014 election until 31 March 2015.

wikipedia-ni-districts.title: List of rural and urban districts in Northern Ireland (Wikipedia)
wikipedia-ni-districts.cites: Craigavon Urban District created in 1967 on the abolition of Lurgan Rural District (1 April 1967), its successor in 1973 Craigavon; Londonderry Rural District reconstituted as an urban district in 1969 (citing Cmd. 534, para. 35); the county boroughs replaced under the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1972 from 1 October 1973, Belfast by the district of Belfast.

wikipedia-belfast-city-council.title: Belfast City Council (Wikipedia)
wikipedia-belfast-city-council.cites: History: the council has its origins in Belfast Corporation; the Lord Mayoralty dates from 1892; the council took its present form after the elections of May 1973 (the Local Government (Modification of Borough Charters) Order (Northern Ireland) 1973 keeps its aldermen); the council elected on 22 May 2014 sat in shadow until it took its powers on 1 April 2015, its district enlarged by parts of Castlereagh, Lisburn and North Down.
